slot.brief: Simplify a compound expression like sin⁻¹x + sin⁻¹y (with a condition on x, y) into a single inverse trig function using standard identities.

stem: For $x,y\ge0$ and $x+y\le1$, simplify $\sin^{-1}x+\sin^{-1}y$ to a single inverse sine.

verdicts.working: Let α = sin⁻¹x and β = sin⁻¹y. Since x + y ≤ 1, x² + y² ≤ 1, so α + β ≤ π/2. Thus sin⁻¹x + sin⁻¹y = sin⁻¹(sin(α + β)) = sin⁻¹(x√(1 − y²) + y√(1 − x²)).

working:
$A=\sin^{-1}x,\ B=\sin^{-1}y;\ \cos(A+B)=\sqrt{1-x^2}\sqrt{1-y^2}-xy\ge0;\ \sin(A+B)=x\sqrt{1-y^2}+y\sqrt{1-x^2};\ A+B=\sin^{-1}(\sin(A+B))$.

Independent check: Let α = sin⁻¹x and β = sin⁻¹y. Since x + y ≤ 1, x² + y² ≤ 1, so α + β ≤ π/2. Thus sin⁻¹x + sin⁻¹y = sin⁻¹(sin(α + β)) = sin⁻¹(x√(1 − y²) + y√(1 − x²)).
